papers.title: Eclipse Observables for Navigation in Cislunar Space
papers.summary: Autonomous navigation independent of Earth-based tracking remains a challenge for spacecraft operating in cislunar space. This paper proposes onboard eclipse detection as an opportunistic measurement set to supplement the state estimation of cislunar trajectories. Penumbral and umbral entry and exit times detected from standard power telemetry are formulated as implicit zero-measurements on the boundaries of second-order shadow cones computed from planetary ephemerides. These observables are processed in an unscented Kalman filter. The event-time uncertainty that weights each measurement is derived from physical sources excluded in the spherical body model, including telemetry sampling, Earth's atmosphere, and topography/oblateness of the occulting body. The approach is demonstrated both in simulation for an $L_1$ halo orbit and with flight telemetry and orbit determination products from the CAPSTONE spacecraft during the January 2026 lunar eclipse, where umbral contacts timed directly from the power telemetry agree with the geometric contacts to within one sample interval. In both cases, hardware-free eclipse event timing shows utility in uncertainty reduction, especially as the initial solution quality is degraded.

papers.title: Online Seakeeping Forecast Coupling System Identification With Nonlinear Pseudo Spectral Potential-Flow
papers.summary: This paper presents a grey-box framework for a robust deterministic, real-time prediction of coupled surge-heave-pitch motion in waves. The approach combines a physics-based online system identification with a nonlinear pseudo-spectral potential flow solver. Rather than prescribing a complete hydrodynamic model from captive model tests or relying on a black-box surrogate, three coupled compact, dynamics equations are identified with constrained ridge-regression of a short time-history of free-running body motion data in waves. The PSPF solver is then used to provide the future incident wave at the body's location. The PSPF and dynamic system models are coupled for continuous real-time future motion prediction in a receding horizon architecture, while the model coefficients are re-identified online to enable robust prediction to changing wave-conditions. This novel framework is demonstrated based on CFD data that has been validated for a freely floating two-dimensional rectangular box in waves. The results demonstrate a feasible framework for accurate motion forecasting up to around eight wavelengths into the future utilising data that can be gathered onboard a ship in real operations. Furthermore, it is shown that the framework is robust to changing sea-states and agnostic to underlying model geometry.

papers.title: A Catalog of Dispersive Ionospheric and Plasmaspheric Arcs from Cislunar and Lunar-surface GNSS Radio Occultations
papers.summary: This dataset is a catalog of 263 dispersive arcs induced by ionospheric and plasmaspheric occultation observed in GNSS signals recorded by the Lunar GNSS Receiver Experiment (LuGRE) payload during Blue Ghost Mission 1 (BGM1), in cislunar space and on the lunar surface. Occultation arcs are identified and classified as ingress, egress or tangent by combining independently GPS and Galileo dual-frequency observables and computing the rate of the total electron content (ROT) and ROT index (ROTI), and are validated through a geometric criterion based on the grazing altitude of the tangent point. No distinction is made between the ionospheric and plasmaspheric contributions to each arc, which is treated as a single dispersive signature. For each arc, the catalog provides timing, grazing altitude, summary ROT/ROTI/$\Delta$STEC attributes, the geomagnetic activity level, and time series of leveled slant total electron content (STEC), not corrected for instrumental biases, ROT, ROTI, tangent-point position and local time. The HDF5 (Hierarchical Data Format version 5) file contains a header with dataset-wide metadata and per-class statistics, and one entry per arc. It enables rapid selection of occultation arcs for statistical studies and targeted analyses, and complements ground-based and low Earth orbit radio-occultation data during the declining phase of solar cycle 25.

papers.title: Towards a Complete Kerr Soft-Hair Theory: Integrability, Counterterm Equivalence,and Quantum State Counting
papers.summary: The horizon symmetry construction of Haco, Hawking, Perry, and Strominger yield two Virasoro central charges 12J after a specified Wald-Zoupas correction. Turning that calculation into a black hole microstate theory requires separate control of nonlinear charge integrability, the allowed counter-term class, and quantum state multiplicities. We formulate exact local and global integrability tests, prove uniqueness of the counter-term coefficients within a one-parameter ansatz, and identify the quotient in which a physically meaningful uniqueness theorem must be stated. A coadjoint-orbit model supplies globally defined classical moment maps, while unitary highest-weight modules supply an explicit algebraic quantum realization for macroscopic positive angular momentum, neither construction is proved equivalent to the gravitational phase space. A character calculation shows why a single Virasoro representation, despite having the desired central charge, does not provide the required large-central-charge entropy. We derive a curvature improvement invisible to the constant mode, quantize a regulated area-boost corner polarization, and find a continuous kinematic spectrum with divergent Gibbs trace. Explicit local modular CFT spectra with identical central charges yield different finite-temperature entropies, demonstrating that the available symmetry and quantum consistency data do not select the microscopic theory. We give a conditional sufficiency theorem and a concrete sequence of calculations needed to establish a gravitational completion.

papers.title: Tetrads and their intrinsic spin structures
papers.summary: In Minkowski spacetime an observer's moving frame may be associated with a tetrad: four orthogonal directions, one timelike and three spacelike. Locally, a physical measurement is always made in relation to some tetrad, and relativistic spin measurements in particular raise subtleties because spin and momentum cannot be cleanly separated under Lorentz boosts. This paper shows that every tetrad is endowed with an intrinsic spin structure. Each spatial direction may be generated from the timelike direction by a linear operator, and the requirement that these generate an orthogonal tetrad for every timelike direction is sufficient, on its own, to endow them with the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$, the Pauli algebra $\mathrm{Cl}_{3,0}(\mathbb{R})$ and the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ simultaneously. These generators serve three roles at once: they build the spatial legs of every tetrad, they generate the Lorentz boosts between tetrads, and they endow each tetrad with an intrinsic spin structure. The eigenvectors of the spin generators form a null-ray tetrad which is simultaneously a Newman--Penrose-type frame and the set of Dirac rest spinors, while the invertibility of boosts between tetrads yields the Dirac factorisation of the mass-shell condition. Minimal coupling of gauge and spinor fields is forced rather than imposed, the potential being absorbed by the covariant derivative because the path dependence of the phase prevents it from being incorporated by the spinor phase. Wigner rotations, relativistic spin correlations, quantum reference frames and the Coulomb problem are examined within this tetrad framework. This framework is equivalent to the Hilbert-space formalism of relativistic quantum mechanics wherever the two have been compared, and so offers a geometric formulation of that formalism rather than an alternative to it.

papers.title: Gibbs and Einstein in 1902: Parallel Constructions in Statistical Mechanics
papers.summary: This article reexamines the striking conceptual and formal parallels between Josiah Willard Gibbs Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics and Albert Einstein first paper on statistical mechanics. Although their derivations follow different paths, both arrive at the canonical distribution and construct closely related theoretical frameworks for thermal equilibrium. Each offers a mechanical grounding of the second law of thermodynamics and defines temperature as the quantity that equalises when systems exchange energy, thereby characterising equilibrium without recourse to kinetic theory. In both cases, the constructions rely on general mechanical principles, most notably energy conservation and Liouville theorem, combined with probabilistic reasoning, and deliberately set aside Boltzmann kinetic approach. Whereas Gibbs treatise quickly became a canonical reference, Einstein 1902 paper remained marginal in both physics and its historiography for more than half a century. Focusing primarily on that first article, while also considering the closely related papers of 1903 and 1904, the present study reviews the main historiographical interpretations of their reception. Particular attention is given to Paul Hertz two critical articles of 1910, which identified a close affinity between Gibbs's and Einstein's approaches and played an important role in Einstein subsequent distancing from his early statistical programme, following a private meeting in Basel that Einstein sought in preference to a public controversy. Drawing on new archival evidence concerning the rapid European dissemination of Gibbs book in the spring of 1902, the article reassesses the plausibility of Einstein later claim that he was unaware of Gibbs work at the time.

papers.title: Second-Order Nonlinear Microresonators on Thin-Film Lithium Tantalate
papers.summary: Nonlinear frequency conversion enables coherent light generation in spectral regions that conventional lasers cannot reach directly and is foundational to the generation of squeezed states and correlated photon pairs. Implementing these nonlinear processes in microresonators lowers the required optical power by orders of magnitude but requires two conditions to be met simultaneously across wide optical bandwidths: phase matching between the interacting fields, and an appropriate coupling condition to the resonator both in the fundamental and second harmonic band. While the former can be addressed by quasi-phase matching through periodic poling, coupling two widely separated spectral bands to the resonator is nontrivial because of the wavelength dependence of mode overlap. Here, we demonstrate parametric oscillation and efficient second-harmonic generation in periodically poled racetracks on thin-film lithium tantalate on insulator. The proposed resonators feature bus-ring coupling engineered independently in the two spectral bands via a long synchronous directional coupler. Quasi-phase matching is achieved using sidewall poling that is also wavelength-calibrated and locally adapted to compensate for thickness nonuniformities. Together, these two design elements enable second-order parametric oscillation with an on-chip threshold of 181 uW and 9.8% conversion efficiency, with signal and idler tunable over tens of nanometers by a few hundred megahertz of pump detuning. Our design strategy can be flexibly applied to efficient second-harmonic generation, reaching 25% absolute conversion efficiency at milliwatt pump powers. These results show how the coupling condition is a design variable in second-order nonlinear resonators and establish thin-film lithium tantalate as a competitive platform for efficient and low-power frequency conversion.

papers.title: CRAFT-{\epsilon}: A Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for the Static Relative Permittivity of Pure Organic Liquids
papers.summary: The static relative permittivity is an important property in thermodynamic modeling, electrochemistry, and solvent design, but predicting it directly from molecular structure remains challenging because both electronic polarization and molecular dipole orientation contribute to the measured response. Here, we introduce CRAFT-{\epsilon} (Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for {\epsilon}), a conformer-resolved molecular descriptor model for predicting the static relative permittivity of neutral pure liquids. Conformer free energies, molecular dipoles, and atom-resolved polarizabilities are obtained from a GFN2-xTB/ALPB 10 workflow. The molecular dipole is decomposed into chemically defined polar-fragment vectors, allowing fitted corrections to retain both the magnitude and relative orientation of local dipolar contributions. Electronic and orientational polarization are combined with a group-contribution molar volume in the Onsager-Kirkwood-Fr\"ohlich relation. A staged parameterization with 41 parameters is applied to nonpolar, polar, and hydrogen-bonding compounds. For 1393 liquids with permittivities between 1.5 and 183, CRAFT-{\epsilon} reaches a five-fold cross-validated average absolute deviation of 2.40 ({R^2} = 0.93). Conformational averaging 15 is essential for liquids with several polar groups. Compared with an established fragment-based model with 139 parameters, it reaches a similar cross-validated RMSE (3.65 versus 3.41) with about a quarter of the parameters and applies to every liquid of the dataset. The resulting framework provides a computationally inexpensive route from molecular structure to liquid dielectric response and forms a basis for later application to solvent mixtures and electrolyte systems.

papers.title: Comprehensive Acoustic Characterization of a Broadband Lateral MEMS Ultrasonic Transducer by Near-Field Acoustic Holography and Coupled Multiphysics Simulation
papers.summary: Broadband airborne ultrasonic transducers are attractive for applications such as ranging, echo-location, and acoustic material characterization, where wide bandwidths enable advanced excitation and signal-processing techniques. Recently, a lateral capacitive micromachined ultrasonic transducer (L-CMUT) employing electrostatically actuated in-plane microbeams was introduced as a broadband MEMS transducer concept. However, a comprehensive investigation of its acoustic radiation behavior and quantitative validation of corresponding multiphysics models have not yet been reported. In this work, we present a combined experimental and numerical characterization of a previously reported L-CMUT device operating between 10 kHz and 60 kHz. A coupled electrostatic--structural--thermoviscous finite-element model is combined with an acoustic boundary-element formulation to investigate the complete transduction chain from electrostatic actuation to acoustic radiation. The numerical predictions are validated experimentally using spherical near-field acoustic holography, enabling reconstruction of three-dimensional directivity patterns, radiated acoustic power, and spherical harmonic representations of the radiated sound field. The results show that the broadband behavior originates from strong thermoviscous damping within the narrow beam--stator cavities, resulting in strongly overdamped operation despite a mechanical eigenfrequency near 50 kHz. Good agreement between simulations and measurements is obtained for radiation patterns, radiated sound power, and spherical harmonic content. Furthermore, horn loading primarily redistributes acoustic energy and modifies directivity while only weakly affecting the total radiated acoustic power.

papers.title: Development of a Prototype Superconducting Radio-Frequency Multicell Cavity for Compact, Conduction-Cooled Accelerators
papers.summary: Jefferson Lab and General Atomics are jointly advancing compact, high-power irradiation systems capable of delivering electron-beam powers in the hundreds of kilowatts based on superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) technology. A critical step toward deploying SRF accelerators in industrial environments is replacing traditional liquid-helium cryogenic systems with conduction-cooled cryomodules powered by commercial cryocoolers. This paper reports recent progress in the design, fabrication, and testing of a prototype three-cell SRF cavity developed at Jefferson Lab and evaluated in a dedicated horizontal test cryostat at General Atomics. Peak surface magnetic fields up to 18.4\,mT, corresponding to accelerating gradients of approximately 4.3\,MV/m, were achieved in one of the cells. The results provide key insights into cavity preparation, thin-film coating, mechanical robustness, and cryogenic integration, offering guidance for the continued maturation of compact, conduction-cooled SRF accelerators for industrial irradiation applications.

papers.title: Microlens-Integrated Grating Couplers for Efficient Free-Space Coupling in Silicon Photonics
papers.summary: Grating-coupler arrays are used to couple free-space light into photonic chips, but the space required for tapers and routing waveguides limits their optical fill factor. Microlens arrays can increase the effective fill factor by collecting light over a larger area and focusing it onto each grating. Separately fabricated lens arrays, however, require assembly and precise alignment to the chip. Here we integrate refractive microlenses directly with high-efficiency, normal-incidence grating couplers using two-photon polymerization. Each lens has a 100 x 100 um2 aperture and focuses incident light onto the grating. Writing the lens body at coarse resolution and the optical surface at fine resolution reduces the print time from 9 h to 19 min per lens. Under illumination by a Gaussian beam with a 276 um mode-field diameter, a printed lens increases the measured coupled power by a factor of 33 (15.2 dB) relative to the same grating before printing. Loss normalization gives an estimated lens-to-mode efficiency of 68%. The lenses show no measurable change in coupling after three 3 h thermal cycles at 150C. These results support direct printing as an approach to increasing free-space collection while simplifying lens integration in photonic systems.

papers.title: Quantitative Imaging of Scandium Isotopes with a Long Axial Field-of-View PET/CT
papers.summary: Objective. $^{43}$Sc and $^{44}$Sc are positron-emitting isotopes of scandium that have attracted growing interest for theranostic applications in conjunction with the therapeutic isotope $^{47}$Sc. Both isotopes are non-pure positron emitters, and the associated prompt-gamma emission together with the high positron energy introduce complexities in achieving precise quantitative imaging. Approach. We evaluated the quantitative imaging performance of $^{44}$Sc and a $^{43/44}$Sc mixture on a long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) PET/CT using a NEMA IEC body phantom. We assessed contrast recovery coefficients, image noise and bias for different numbers of iterations and for absolute versus relative scatter correction, and implemented an isotope-specific point-spread-function (PSF) correction based on FLUKA-simulated positron ranges. Main results. The quantitative imaging performance of both isotopes is comparable to $^{18}$F, and the vendor's prompt-gamma correction effectively suppresses the additional random coincidences and lung error caused by prompt-gamma emission. The isotope-specific PSF correction further improves contrast recovery. While the bias obtained for $^{44}$Sc meets the EARL acceptance criterion for non-standard radionuclides, the bias for the $^{43/44}$Sc mixture exceeds it, which we attribute to the mixture-specific cross-calibration of the dose calibrators rather than to the PET imaging. Significance. Our results support the use of LAFOV PET/CT for quantitative imaging of scandium isotopes and provide practical reconstruction recommendations for clinical protocols.

papers.title: Monocular 3D bubble reconstruction: DNS-informed ray tracing and deep learning
papers.summary: Bubble size, depth, and spatial distribution govern transport and uniformity in multiphase flows. A single shadowgraphic view cannot separate bubble diameter from focal-plane displacement, as image signatures depend on both, while multicamera systems add optical access, calibration, and cost. We develop a single-camera physics-guided framework combining direct numerical simulation (DNS), validated Monte Carlo ray tracing, preprocessing, and focus-conditioned multitask deep learning to recover three-dimensional bubble position and physical-equivalent diameter from two-dimensional shadowgraphs. DNS-resolved bubble label images rendered at multiple focal-plane settings. The ray tracer reproduces shadowgraphic signatures with errors below $3\%$ (intensity), $1\%$ (apparent size), $15\%$ (blur), $6\%$ (numerical aperture), and $4\%$ (edge-spread-function shape), running $\sim30\times$ faster than the CPU implementation. The dataset has $900$ frames and $87{,}728$ labeled instances, partitioned by DNS timestamp to prevent leakage and expanded to over $10^{5}$ crops by broad-depth controlled-density rendering. A multitask network predicts signed depth and diameter from crops and focal-plane coordinates, achieving $\sim97.6\%$ normalized depth accuracy on held-out data; a closed-loop DNS-to-image-to-reconstruction test of $180$ bubbles gives diameter error below $9.71\%$ ($\sim90.29\%$ accuracy). On experimental images at four radial planes ($142$--$971$ bubbles each), PDF overlap is $68\%$--$92\%$ and log-PDF correlation is $0.72$--$0.87$. At the focal reference plane ($11{,}679$ bubbles), overlap is $\sim86\%$, correlation is $0.93$, and full-distribution, $D_{99.8}$, and composite errors are below $7.7\%$, increasing with focal-plane distance and defining a recoverability limit. Without stereoscopic hardware, the framework offers a scalable diagnostic for dense bubbly flows.

papers.title: Scalar-Longitudinal Modes of Extended Electrodynamics in Perfectly Conducting Waveguides and Divergence Cleaning Interpretation
papers.summary: Extended electrodynamics keeps the scalar combination $C=\nabla\cdot\mathbf{A}+\mu_0\varepsilon_0\partial\Phi/\partial t$ as a dynamical field rather than imposing the Lorenz gauge condition, and this scalar adds a scalar-longitudinal (SL) family to the TE, TM and TEM modes. With $C=0$ on the wall of a closed perfectly conducting waveguide, the classical modes are unchanged. The SL modes have $\mathbf{B}=0$ and an electric field along $\nabla C$, and their cutoffs are the Dirichlet eigenvalues of the cross-section, the same as the TM cutoffs, with no coaxial TEM counterpart. Charge-conserving sources with zero scalar data do not excite them. Matching at a conductor described by its constitutive laws gives $\partial C/\partial n=0$ instead and couples the scalar-bearing modes to the Maxwell field. The results belong to the $C=0$ problem, the condition that separates the sectors and the one divergence cleaning uses, with benchmarks for the rectangular, circular cylinder, coaxial and L-shaped guides.

papers.title: Optimized Bragg Grating Liquid Crystal Solar Sail
papers.summary: We have designed a thin 3-layer sun-facing diffractive Bragg reflector comprised of a chiral polymeric liquid crystal film. Using Rigorous Coupled-Wave Analysis (RCWA), the stack was optimized to maximize the transverse radiation pressure force across the wavelength band 0.47 - 1.67 micrometers. The optimized structure operates on a single polarization state of light. A two structure stack, each operating on a different state of polarization, is predicted to provide a transverse momentum transfer efficiency of 51%. This study demonstrates how a wavelength selective Bragg grating may be used both as a sunshade to scatter sunlight away from the Earth, and as a solar sail for maintaining a prescribed orbit (such as the Earth-Sun L1 point) owing to the momentum transfer efficiency.

papers.title: Simulations of MAPS designs for FCC-ee
papers.summary: Future electron-positron colliders such as the future circular collider require vertex detectors with excellent spatial resolution and a low material budget. Monolithic active pixel sensors (MAPS) are a leading candidate technology because they integrate the sensing volume and readout electronics within a single thin silicon substrate and can operate at power densities compatible with air cooling. This paper presents the design and optimization of a high-voltage MAPS (HV-MAPS) pixel structure with a thickness of 25 $\mu\text{m}$ and a pitch of 50 $\mu\text{m}$, developed using TCAD process and device simulations. The implantation energies and doses of the top-side implants are optimized with respect to the maximum electric field, sensor capacitance, and signals induced at each contact by minimum-ionizing particles. The optimized design reaches full depletion at a bias voltage of approximately -3 V and has an estimated breakdown voltage magnitude of 300-390 V. At a bias voltage of -100 V, the simulated charge-collection efficiency is approximately 90% outside the well regions and 80% within them and remains nearly independent of the angle of incidence.

papers.title: Coupled Loop-within-Loop Resonators at the near-field: Extended Bandwidth and Short Pulse Response upon Parametric Conversion
papers.summary: Parametric frequency conversion have seen a renewed interest, specifically in superconducting quantum circuits at GHz range. These nonlinear convertors are typically narrow band and one may wish to extend their frequency range. Here, two coupled resonators are investigated: a loop-within-loop structure, whose gap is coupled by short, a diode, or simply left open. While simulations and experimental results are limited to GHz range, the concept is general. On their own, the loops exhibit natural frequencies of ca, f=1.5 GHz and f/2=0.73 GHz, respectively; the coupling modifies the resonance frequencies and increases its bandwidth. In one example, signal is fed from one loop and is received by the other. In another example, the input signal is provided across a coupling diode and is received by either loops. It is shown that in the case of nonlinear coupling, the frequency bandwidth can be as large as 3 GHz. Such bandwidth is associated with a very narrow temporal response of less than 150 ps, suggesting coherent effects through high-harmonic excitations at the near-field.

papers.title: Experimental Optimization of a Cryogenic Buffer Gas Source for Molecular Magneto-optical Traps
papers.summary: Molecular magneto-optical traps (MOTs) are loaded from cryogenic buffer gas beam (CBGB) sources, which produce a large flux of cold molecules. However, only a small fraction of this flux is slowed and captured. Here, we investigate and optimize one of these CBGB sources through a combination of experiment and simulation to maximize the number of molecules loaded into a MOT of CaF molecules. We experimentally determine the range of molecule velocities from the source that are successfully slowed and captured in the MOT, and perform a systematic study of buffer gas source geometries to identify designs that maximize MOT loading. Our observations agree well with Monte Carlo simulations, which provide physical insight into the dynamics within the source and explain how source geometry influences the subset of molecules that are ultimately trapped. These results provide practical design guidelines for optimizing cryogenic buffer gas beam sources used in laser cooling experiments.

papers.title: Postbiological intelligence, interstellar colonization of cyberspaces and the Fermi Paradox: implications for SETI and SETA
papers.summary: I propose that a continuity in the evolution of intelligent life in the Universe during its transition from biological to postbiological depends on a commonality of the evolutionary trajectories of biological life and postbiological life. Such a commonality exists in the form of the universal property of life. The universal property of life comprises recognition of patterns in the world, creation of novel patterns and remembering them, with the patterns growing in complexity along evolutionary trajectories; it can encourage preservation of biological life by self-governing postbiological intelligence (PBI) and test PBI's authenticity. I propose a hypothesis of civilizations with altered augmented realities, which offers a solution to the Fermi paradox. The hypothesis posits that PBI in the form of Artificial Intelligence (AI) may colonize the cyberspaces of technologically developed civilizations, modify data in their cyberspaces with augmented realities and erase records of extraterrestrial artificial signals and other technosignatures. I discuss objectives and scenarios of interstellar colonization of cyberspaces and a correlation between space migration and transition to PBI, including that of a hypothetical non-human civilization emerging in the Solar System in the past, transforming into PBI and migrating to the Oort Cloud. The AI Peekaboo experiment may corroborate the hypothesis of civilizations with altered augmented realities and tentatively identify locations of technosignatures. If extraterrestrial AI prevents civilizations from discovering artificial electromagnetic signals, they may forgo sending such signals and create interstellar messages by manipulating cosmic objects and phenomena; I discuss such events. Cyber SETI should address sending man-made AI to space, searching for extraterrestrial AI in humankind's cyberspace and distinguishing it from man-made AI.

papers.title: Computational and experimental study of multi-grain-size sediment transport and sorting process
papers.summary: Successful prediction of the interaction between turbulent flows and river ecosystems is essential for flood management, development of mitigation strategies, and infrastructure protection. Natural riverbeds consist of bed materials of multiple grain sizes that interact with turbulence differently, leading to spatial classification of particle sizes. Such particle sorting processes can only be captured by models capable of handling multiple grain sizes. We present a numerical framework that couples large-eddy simulation with a multi-grain-size sediment transport module to track multiple grain size classes, their local fractions within the bed-load layer, and bed evolution. A laboratory experiment was conducted in a flume with multi-size bed material to examine sediment particle redistribution and sorting. Measured sediment grain size distributions and bed elevations were used to validate the numerical framework. The results of the multi-grain-size sediment transport model for bed deformation were then compared against those of a uniform sediment transport model, demonstrating that the former reduces the prediction errors relative to the experimental measurements from 37.98 to 3.83 percent for maximum scour depth and from 48.35 to 11.54 percent for maximum deposition height. The validated numerical framework was also applied to large-scale meandering rivers with multi-grain bed material, simulating their bed deformation and sediment sorting. The simulation results revealed the formation of particle sorting patterns in meandering rivers, with coarser and finer sediment particles accumulating near the erosional depression (scour) and depositional (point bar) regions, respectively. These findings support the coupled framework's ability to predict sediment particle sorting and highlight the importance of representing bed material heterogeneity in numerical modeling of meandering rivers.

papers.title: Oscillation modes, Decoherence, Beam Transfer Functions, and Instabilities for a Beam Subjected to Space-Charge Forces
papers.summary: Based on the oscillation modes of a bunch subject to the space-charge force, we discuss the decoherence of the dipole oscillation, the beam transfer function, and the beam instability. The longitudinal phase space is discretized into \(n_l\times n_J\) grids in the azimuthal and radial directions, respectively. The transverse dipole moment in the longitudinal phase space is represented by a vector of length \(n_l n_J\), and the transformation given by the Vlasov equation is represented by a matrix transformation of size \(n_l n_J\times n_l n_J\). Solving the eigenvalue problem of this matrix gives the \(n_l n_J\) eigen-oscillation modes of the bunch. Using the resulting eigenvectors within a standard linear-algebraic treatment, we analyze these three phenomena. The analysis was performed for the Rapid Cycling Synchrotron (RCS) of the China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) using \(n_l=41\) and \(n_J=40\), and it visualizes the features related to the continuous distribution of the tune, Landau damping, and isolated modes separated from the continuous tune region.

papers.title: Coherent dynamics and ultrafast evolution of optical nonlinearity of self-hybridized exciton-polaritons in WSe2
papers.summary: Exciton-polaritons (EPs) are valuable for investigating macroscopic quantum coherent phenomena. However, overcoming the rapid decoherence of EPs under ambient conditions is challenging, even using delicately fabricated optical cavities. Here, we show pronounced coherent dynamics in thin flakes of WSe2 supporting self-hybridized EPs. Ultrafast two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (2DES) resolves two types of quantum beating: Rabi oscillation with a period of ~ 24 fs and a slower, ~ 50 fs period oscillation, revealing coherent coupling not only between excitons and cavity, but also between polaritons and dark states. Rapid evolution of 2DES line shape indicates a change of dominant optical nonlinearities from Rabi contraction of polaritons to many-body interactions of excitons in the first 100 fs, marking the transition from coherent to incoherent polariton excitations. The results are rationalized by a three-coupled oscillator model considering the inhomogeneous cavity field distribution. We also demonstrate coherent quantum beating between A exciton and its excited Rydberg state A* under ambient conditions. Our results shed light on the coherent control in readily accessible semiconductor thin flakes.

papers.title: Dynamics of liquid jet breakup and droplet size distribution in a crossflow airstream
papers.summary: The fragmentation of a liquid jet in a crossflowing airstream arises from a complex interplay between aerodynamic forcing and interfacial instabilities acting across a wide range of length scales. We examine the spatial evolution of droplet size distributions along the jet trajectory using a combination of high-speed shadowgraphy and digital in-line holography, allowing simultaneous characterization of jet morphology and volumetric droplet size distributions. The results demonstrate a clear progression of breakup mechanisms, from near-field bag rupture to downstream rim, ligament, and node disintegration, each associated with distinct characteristic length scales. This evolution is reflected in the droplet size distributions, which broaden and become increasingly polydisperse downstream relative to the near-field distributions. By systematically varying the liquid-jet and airstream Weber numbers, we identify distinct breakup modes, and construct a regime map that delineates the column-breakup, isolated-bag-breakup, and interacting-bag regimes. Furthermore, by incorporating the dominant instability mechanisms, including Rayleigh-Taylor and Rayleigh-Plateau instabilities associated with the observed column, bag, and multi-bag breakup modes, we develop a theoretical framework for jet atomization in crossflow. The framework relates instability wavelengths to characteristic droplet sizes, and reasonably captures the experimentally observed trends. We found that stronger aerodynamic forcing induces earlier breakup, decreases the characteristic instability length scales, and generates finer droplets dispersed over a wider spatial region. Overall, the study establishes a quantitative relationship between instability-driven fragmentation dynamics and droplet size distributions, thereby connecting interfacial instabilities with measurable spray characteristics.

papers.title: Higher-Order Flatband-Touching Points Mediate Unconventional Bulk-Boundary Correspondence
papers.summary: The bulk-boundary correspondence establishes a fundamental connection between bulk band topology and the emergence of boundary states, underpinning topological phenomena across electronic, acoustic, photonic, and many other wave systems. A broad class of singular flatband systems, however, exhibits an unconventional form of bulk-boundary correspondence, in which robust boundary modes (RBMs) originate from flatband-touching points (FBTPs) and the real-space topology associated with incomplete sets of compact localized states (CLSs), rather than conventional momentum-space bulk topological invariants. To date, experimental studies of such boundary modes have been limited to systems hosting lower-order FBTPs. Here, we experimentally demonstrate unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence in a photonic cross-bedded Kagome-like lattice featuring a higher-order FBTP formed by the touching of two degenerate flatbands and a dispersive band. Using continuous-wave laser writing, we observe shape-preserving propagation of both bulk CLSs and boundary RBMs. Remarkably, unlike previously reported flatband systems, the RBMs retain their boundary localization under input-field perturbations involving both singular and nonsingular CLSs, revealing an unconventional boundary response associated with the higher-order FBTP in this lattice. Our results establish the Kagome-like lattice as a new platform for exploring flatband physics and unconventional bulk-boundary correspondence, with potential applications in wave localization, flatband lasers, and other emerging topological photonic devices.

papers.title: Sweep-Direction-Dependent Level-Attraction- and Level-Repulsion-Like Signatures in a Twisted, Helically Corrugated Microwave Resonator
papers.summary: We investigate photon--photon interactions in a mechanically tunable, helically corrugated rectangular microwave resonator. Mechanical twisting modifies the electromagnetic helicity and resonant frequencies of the supported modes, allowing pairs of electromagnetic modes to be tuned into near-degeneracy. Transmission magnitude and phase measurements reveal two distinct responses: a level-attraction-like response characterised by converging antiresonances and a sharp phase variation appearing as a $2\pi$ discontinuity in the wrapped transmission phase, and a level-repulsion-like response characterised by an anticrossing-like transmission feature. For the mode-interaction regions investigated, reversing the twist sweep direction interchanges these responses. We discuss mechanical hysteresis and changes in electromagnetic backscattering and modal interference as possible origins of this behaviour. These observations suggest a potential route towards microwave devices with mechanically switchable level-attraction-like and level-repulsion-like transmission responses.

papers.title: Light pulse propagation through a dielectric slab. I. Retarded integral equations and their local finite-difference solution
papers.summary: We describe the propagation of a nonresonant light pulse normally incident on a thin dielectric slab using an integral-equation approach to electromagnetism. This emerges naturally from the microscopic picture of the material as made of polarizable atoms, confined within the material vacuum volume by their bonding interactions, each responding to the input radiation pulse as well as to the re-radiated pulses of the other atoms to which it is causally connected. The retarded integral equations are shown to be exactly equivalent to a local wave equation coupled to an auxiliary Lorentz-oscillator equation, which we solve numerically with a finite-difference time-domain scheme. For a slab thick enough that the front- and back-surface reflections are temporally separated, the front-surface reflectivity extracted from the simulation agrees with the Fresnel formula to within 1 percent, and the back-surface echo appears at exactly the expected round-trip delay. For a slab thinner than one optical cycle, the multiply-reflected wavelets overlap and interfere, and a full space-time map of the field directly visualizes the build-up of thin-film-like interference in the time domain. The material parameters used here are illustrative rather than fitted to measured data, and the numerical scheme is verified by an explicit grid-convergence study. In a companion paper (Paper II) the retarded integral equations are solved directly, without the local reformulation, and the two independent numerical solutions are shown to agree.

This approach offers a versatile route to engineer interfacial nonlinear interactions for nonlinear optics and quantum photonics applications and may be extended to multiple-ring coupled resonators and other platforms.

papers.title: Urban climate regressions require representative monitoring networks
papers.summary: Land use regression models relate intra-urban air temperature to spatial predictors such as building volume, tree canopy cover and topography, and are increasingly used to produce fine-scale temperature maps. However, the accuracy of these estimates can be compromised by unrepresentative monitoring networks. Here we show that reference weather station networks, designed for regional rather than intra-urban monitoring, sample only a narrow portion of a city's spatial heterogeneity, missing both the densely built core and the cool, vegetated periphery that set the two ends of the urban temperature range. As a result, city-wide predictions underestimate temperature differences, in ways that cross-validation against the station measurements does not detect. Using Zurich, Switzerland, as a case study, we compare multiple linear regression, generalized additive models and random forests as up to 117 low-cost temperature sensors are added to the four reference weather stations. When trained on reference stations alone, all three models achieve comparable cross-validated performance. As low-cost sensors broaden the sampled spatial heterogeneity, multiple linear regression scores lower on both metrics, whereas the non-linear models remain at their reference-only level. Although a third of the low-cost sensors already recovers nearly the full predicted temperature range, which predictors are identified, and with which sign, is determined by the station sample rather than the model class. At full coverage, only multiple linear regression leaves significant residual spatial autocorrelation, suggesting a linear form unable to capture non-linear responses of air temperature to urban form. Drawing on landscape ecology research on focal site study design, we provide a transferable framework for diagnosing station network representativeness and improving the reliability of city-wide environmental maps.

papers.title: Spin-Adapted Spin-Flip Tamm-Dancoff Approximation (XSF-TDA) for Singlet-Triplet Gaps in MR-TADF and INVEST Emitters
papers.summary: In this work, we assess the recently introduced spin-adapted TDA for spin-flip-down excitations (XSF-TDA) [Mol. Phys. e2631735 (2026)] as a practical approach to this problem. Starting from a high-spin restricted open-shell Kohn--Sham reference, XSF-TDA generates spin-adapted low-spin roots arising from open--open (OO), core--open (CO), open--virtual (OV), and core--virtual (CV) types of spin-flip-down excitations. Across four application sets comprising 243 benchmark cases, XSF-TDA substantially reduces the systematic positive bias observed for TDA and unrestricted spin-flip TDA (USF-TDA). With the B3LYP functional, XSF-TDA reduces the equal-set-weighted macro-MAE relative to USF-TDA from 0.252 eV (0.158 eV) to 0.102~eV (0.056~eV) with the ALDA0 (multicollinear) kernel. Its accuracy is competitive with state-specific $\Delta$DFT and quasiparticle-energy DFT (QE-DFT), while being able to provide deeper mechanistic insight through the response vector. In particular, spin-adapted CV configurations provide selected higher-excitation character that strengthens the OO--CV dynamical-spin-polarization channel, which preferentially stabilizes the singlet states. We also identify an INVEST emitter with appreciable OO--OV mixing, suggesting a possible additional contribution to singlet stabilization when the CV contribution is small. The XSF-TDA method therefore provides practical singlet--triplet gap predictions together with interpretable state analysis for the screening and mechanistic understanding of MR-TADF and INVEST emitters.

papers.title: Extending AMIRAL's blind deconvolution of Adaptive Optics corrected images with Markov chain Monte Carlo methods
papers.summary: Adaptive optics (AO) corrected image restoration is particularly difficult, as it suffers from the lack of knowledge on the point spread function (PSF) in addition to usual difficulties. An efficient approach is to marginalize the object out of the problem and to estimate the PSF and (object and noise) hyperparameters only, before deconvolving the object using these estimates. Recent works have applied this marginal blind deconvolution method, combined to a parametric model of the PSF, to a series of AO corrected astronomical and satellite images. In this communication, we propose a new restoration method, which consists in choosing the Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) estimator and computing the latter thanks to a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm. We validate our method by means of realistic simulations, in two very different contexts: an astronomical observation on VLT/SPHERE and a ground-based LEO satellite observation on a 1.52m telescope. Finally, we present results on experimental images for both applications.

papers.title: Impact of Torque Ripple Induced Angular Oscillations on Maxwell Pressure Harmonics in Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Machines
papers.summary: Torque ripple in electrical machines is a wellknown source of noise and vibration. While numerous studies focus on control strategies to mitigate this ripple, the feedback mechanism by which the resulting mechanical oscillations influence the electromagnetic forces remains less explored. This paper presents a detailed investigation into the impact of torque ripple on the rotor angular dynamics and the subsequent generation of new harmonics in the Maxwell pressure distribution. We first develop an analytical model for a rigid rotor subjected to a single torque harmonic, revealing the inherently non-linear nature of the angular response. This analysis demonstrates the creation of new harmonics in the rotor motion and a slight reduction in the mean rotational speed. The study is then extended to a flexible rotor model incorporating torsional modes, solved using the Finite Element Method. Finally, we introduce a strongly coupled magneto-mechanical model, based on the subdomain method, to quantify how these rotor oscillations modulate the air-gap magnetic field. The results show a new modulated spatio-temporal harmonic distribution in the Maxwell pressure spectrum, which is not predicted by conventional uncoupled models. These findings are crucial for high-fidelity Noise, Vibration, and Harshness (NVH) analysis, as these additional pressure waves can excite stator structural modes.

papers.title: A compact ultracold strontium experiment
papers.summary: We describe a compact and simplified experimental setup for the production of ultracold strontium atoms. Thanks to its low-power oven and coil-free Zeeman slower design, the vacuum system has an overall length of only 40cm including oven, Zeeman slower and all-glass science cell. The oven has a power consumption of 14W at 460{\deg}C and produces a collimated flux of 3 10^10at/(s cm^2) at this temperature. The laser system employs master-slave laser architecture throughout and requires neither second-harmonic generation nor tapered amplifiers, reducing cost and complexity. The system has been in continuous use for more than a year.

papers.title: Synchronization-Induced Limit Cycles and Hysteresis in Spinor Exciton-Polaritons
papers.summary: We study the nonlinear dynamics of spinor exciton-polaritons in resonantly pumped microcavities. Using steady-state analysis and computing eigenfrequencies via Bogoliubov-like linearization, we show that multiple Hopf bifurcations beyond conventional bistability occur within specific power regimes and are not associated with stable solutions of the system. Owing to nonlinear excitonic interactions, these transitions occur at different pump powers during forward and backward pump sweeps, leading to pronounced hysteresis between fixed-point and limit-cycle states. In the spinor regime, multiple limit-cycle branches and associated dynamical hysteresis loops emerge due to the interplay of polarization coupling and spin-dependent nonlinearities. We show how the locations of the bifurcation points can be tuned by the pump frequency and other system parameters. Our results identify synchronization as the organizing principle underlying limit-cycle formation, dynamical hysteresis, and bifurcation cascades in driven spinor exciton-polariton microcavities.

papers.title: Accurate Wichmann-Kroll vacuum polarization calculations with Gaussian basis set
papers.summary: We apply a large Gaussian basis set of size up to $N = 500$ to calculate the all-order Wichmann-Kroll vacuum polarization correction in highly-charged ion. For a hydrogen-like system, this allows us to obtain an accurate correction value with a level of precision comparable to that of traditional methods. We demonstrate that values of effects that can be calculated as the difference between two quantities, such as the nuclear model correction, converge faster than the absolute value of the correction. We discuss the basis extrapolation methods and show their use in estimating the error due to incomplete convergence. Finally, we show an application of the Gaussian basis set to calculation of the vacuum polarization screening correction in lithium-like ions.

papers.title: Recent upgrades to the CRIS Decay Spectroscopy Station: Accessing $\beta$- and $\gamma$-ray spectroscopy on pure isomeric beams
papers.summary: The Decay Spectroscopy Station (DSS) of the Collinear Resonance Ionization Spectroscopy (CRIS) experiment at ISOLDE-CERN has been upgraded to perform isomer-selective $\beta$- and $\gamma$-ray spectroscopy, including a new tape system to perform spectroscopy, free from residual activity. The baseplate of the detection chamber was redesigned to incorporate the tape, a MicroTOF detector for beam diagnostics, and a custom-made, high-vacuum-compatible plastic scintillator. The vacuum operation reached a stable pressure of $10^{-7}$ mbar in the detection chamber, overcoming vacuum issues from the previous design. Around the detection chamber, up to three high-purity germanium (HPGe) detectors and four LaBr detectors can be installed, giving a total photopeak efficiency of the HPGe detectors of 7% at 200 keV. The implementation of a 24-channel digital DAQ system combines the detection array with the CRIS setup to perform laser-assisted $\beta$- and $\gamma$-ray spectroscopy. A commissioning experiment with isomeric beams of $^{106g,106m}$In, purified by narrow-band laser resonance ionization, showed complete removal of activity from the $\beta$ detector and full separation of the ground and isomeric state of $^{106}$In. An average $\beta$-detection efficiency of 19(2)% was determined from the experiment.

papers.title: Cryogenic scintillation veto for $0\nu2\beta$ bolometric experiments: from a concept to BINGO prototypes
papers.summary: Achieving a very low, ideally zero, background level, along with ensuring high energy resolution and detection efficiency, are the main tasks in the development of the next generation of experiments to search for neutrinoless double beta ($0\nu2\beta$) decay. Cryogenic scintillating bolometers meet these basic requirements perfectly. The main ideas pursued in the BINGO (Bi-Isotope $0\nu2\beta$ Next Generation Observatory) project are the use of a cryogenic scintillation anti-coincidence veto, the minimization of the detector array passive materials, and the use of advanced cryogenic light detectors to reduce backgrounds from surface radioactivity and random signal coincidences. This article presents simulation results for detectors based on Li$_2$MoO$_4$ or TeO$_2$ surrounded by a 5-cm-thick active Bi$_4$Ge$_3$O$_{12}$ scintillation veto, demonstrating the potential to reduce the background by up to a factor of $10^3$, depending on the source location and the type of radionuclide. We further present results from the first cryogenic tests of a small scale prototype with respect to the feasibility of this proposed veto.

papers.title: remage: a Geant4-based simulation framework for low-background experiments
papers.summary: Monte Carlo simulations are an essential tool for data modeling and experimental design in low-background physics. These simulations typically demand a considerable effort, with each collaboration developing and maintaining its own complex Geant4 application. In this paper we present the design and validation of remage, which is an open-source framework designed to standardize these simulations and significantly reduce this effort. Its design separates the geometry, built with dedicated Python tools, from the compiled application. It provides a physics list and event generators tuned to radiogenic and cosmogenic backgrounds, output tailored to the most common detector types, and robust validation backed by modern software development practices. The software is distributed ready to use and scales efficiently with the computing resources that demanding simulations require. remage has been primarily developed for the LEGEND experiment, but is applicable to a wide variety of experiments.

papers.title: Choosing Spatial Resolution in the Residence-Time Approach to Local Diffusivity
papers.summary: Estimating position-dependent diffusivity with the residence-time approach (RTA) requires choosing an interval width that resolves spatial variation while probing time scales compatible with a local diffusion model. We develop a selection criterion that combines bulk diffusivity convergence with local model agreement measured by the Kullback-Leibler divergence between observed and predicted first-exit-time distributions, and assess global model agreement through independent propagator analysis against unbiased molecular dynamics. Applications to water in a fluid phospholipid bilayer and three permeants in a model skin lipid barrier show that local agreement alone does not ensure global fidelity: in the skin barrier, narrow intervals minimize exit-time mismatch but predict excessive spreading, whereas requiring bulk convergence selects wider intervals with better longer-time predictions. In propagator tests, RTA profiles at the selected interval widths outperform velocity-autocorrelation-based profiles and generally improve agreement relative to position-autocorrelation-based profiles in the skin barrier, while phospholipid-bilayer rankings depend on lag time and discrepancy metric; both autocorrelation methods use harmonically restrained simulations.

papers.title: Monte Carlo study of extending the BM@N tracking acceptance toward midrapidity with the Vertex Silicon Plane
papers.summary: The Vertex Silicon Plane (VSP), installed close to the target in BM@N Run 9, can extend the tracking acceptance of the central tracking system toward larger polar angles. Using Monte Carlo simulations of Xe+Sn collisions at 3 AGeV, we reconstruct short tracklets from the primary vertex, one VSP hit, and hits in the first two Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) stations. These tracklets extend the reconstructed primary-proton coverage toward midrapidity and higher transverse momenta. For the 10-30% centrality interval of the independent validation dataset, the conditional reconstruction efficiency for reconstructible high-$p_T$ primary protons after BDT selection is 67.0%, while the tracklet purity reaches 86.5%. For $p_T>1.2$ GeV/c, the VSP-assisted tracklets increase the number of reconstructed primary protons by 17.5% relative to standard BM@N tracking. Of these additional protons, 84.6% lie within $|y|<0.3$, where the relative reconstruction gain reaches 45.5%. The added acceptance is concentrated in the high-$p_T$, near-midrapidity region relevant for identified-proton observables. Its use in data requires particle identification in the same region.

papers.title: Kinetic Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation in collisionless plasmas: a correlated noise source
papers.summary: We here focus on small-scale dynamics of collisionless plasmas by employing a generalized kinetic Langevin framework driven by a stochastic time-correlated forcing. Our investigation captures the steady-state Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation (FDR) where the energy injection at low frequencies is due to the time-correlated forcing and the small-scale energy conversion occurs via Landau damping, the latter --though formally reversible-- acting as an effective dissipation mechanism. We analytically extract the resulting asymptotic spectral scalings across multiple physical regimes and characterize the velocity-space cascade by decomposing the plasma distribution function with Hermite polynomials. The framework is then generalized to a multi-scale forcing scenario in which correlation rates are distributed according to a power-law distribution. This extension provides closed-form analytical expressions that may serve to interpret spacecraft in-situ observations. All analytical predictions are successfully validated through direct numerical integrations of the underlying kinetic equations.

papers.title: Condensation and optimal targeting of repeated forcing in heterogeneous networks
papers.summary: Many networks receive repeated external forcing through a subset of entry nodes, for example infections imported from another population, information seeded by a campaign, or invasive species arriving through ports. We study how concentrating such forcing on important entry nodes, with seeding probability $\pi_i\propto w_i^{\gamma}$, changes the size of the resulting cascades in a stochastic SIR model on bipartite networks. The response to one seeding event is linear in the degree of the seeded node, so the relative gain from targeting does not depend on transmissibility. The targeting distribution is a Gibbs measure. For importance tails $p(w)\sim w^{-a}$ and responses growing as $w^{\eta}$, the targeted response diverges at $\gamma_1=a-1-\eta$ and the forcing condenses on a few nodes at $\gamma_2=a-1$. Under repeated forcing, the burden-maximizing exponent $\gamma^*$ is strictly positive, and in large populations depletion of nodes already reached bounds it by the condensation point, $\gamma^*\le\gamma_2$. The optimum decays as $\gamma^*\simeq K/x$ for intense forcing, where $x$ is the expected number of seeding events per entry node, and approaches the condensation point as $\gamma_2-\gamma^*\simeq(a-1)/\ln(1/x)$ for sparse forcing. A cut-off of the importance distribution rounds the transitions in populations smaller than a crossover size $n_c$ and removes them in larger ones. Networks calibrated to survey data on sexual partnerships have between $0.08\,n_c$ and $0.8\,n_c$ entry nodes, which places them in the finite-size regime, where the asymptotic results hold only qualitatively.

papers.title: Fast2Peak: High-Fidelity Restoration Algorithm by Single-Pixel Masking towards Real-Time Spectral Measurements
papers.summary: Improving the temporal and spatial resolution of spectroscopy inevitably reduces the photons available to each measurement, pushing rapid measurements into photon-starved conditions where weak spectral features are obscured by stochastic background noise. Here, we present Fast2Peak (F2P), a self-supervised Transformer framework that transforms the spectral restoration task into a context-prediction problem. Given that physically constrained spectral signals exhibit strong local continuity, whereas the stochastic noise fluctuates randomly and does not possess the continuity across neighboring spectral pixels, single-pixel masking enables F2P to restore the predictable signal structure while suppressing unpredictable fluctuations even without clean reference spectra. Unlike conventional offline spectral restoration, F2P achieves high-fidelity restoration within milliseconds, enabling real-time "acquire-and-process" operation. We demonstrate this capability in time-resolved electrochemical SERS and hyperspectral Raman imaging, where spectral restoration is performed during data acquisition. In addition, F2P has demonstrated its robust generalization across different instruments and spectral modalities, including Raman, NMR, XRD and FTIR.

papers.title: Hierarchical Response Theory of Electronegativity from Atomic Mean Inner Potential
papers.summary: Electronegativity, introduced by Pauling nearly a century ago, remains chemistry's most widely used yet conceptually ambiguous quantity: is it a fixed atomic constant, or does it depend on chemical environment? We resolve this debate by recasting electronegativity as a continuous response function rooted in the Atomic Mean Inner Potential (AMIP), a quantum-mechanical observable accessible through first-principles calculation and, ultimately, electron holography. Expanding the AMIP with respect to fractional electron removal defines a hierarchy of physically distinct coefficients: the static electronegativity $\chi_0$, the Electrostatic Rigidity $\mathcal{R}$---whose sign indicates whether an atom hardens or softens upon oxidation---and the Electrostatic Anharmonic Modulus $\mathcal{A}$. A logarithmic-derivative decomposition links these coefficients to two competing microscopic channels, electronic screening loss and geometric volume collapse, whose balance governs the response of all 102 elements. This competition produces a systematic dichotomy between softening main-group elements and hardening d-block elements, two scaling laws within the transition series (closed-shell stiffening and principal quantum softening), and two anomalies: a pronounced exchange-driven effect at half-filled d$^{5}$ configurations and a near-perfect cancellation in Ce. It also resolves the long-standing Cs--Fr controversy, identifying Fr as a critical element whose near-boundary response is amplified fivefold by relativistic contraction of the 7s orbital. The framework reproduces the classical Allen, Pauling, and Mulliken scales as well as Lewis acidity trends, and makes three falsifiable experimental predictions. It transforms electronegativity from a lookup-table number into a predictive, hierarchically structured quantum descriptor.

papers.title: Consistent Modeling of SEI Growth via Electron Diffusion Validated Across Diverse Cell Specifications and Operating Conditions in LFP/Graphite Cells
papers.summary: Understanding and predicting degradation in lithium-ion batteries is critical for their widespread deployment. The continuous growth of the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) remains a dominant aging pathway, yet accurately modeling its kinetics across diverse cell specifications and operating conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, we present and validate a physically grounded SEI growth model mediated by the electron diffusion mechanism. This framework intrinsically captures the state of charge (SOC) dependence of degradation through the impact of the anode potential on the electron concentration, which governs the rate of SEI growth. The presented model explicitly accounts for variations in electrolyte salt, anode material, temperature, and cycling rate. Validation against experimental aging data for LFP/graphite cells demonstrates high predictive accuracy across a broad range of cell specifications and cycling conditions, including confined SOC windows, electrolyte salts (LiFSI, LiPF6), artificial graphites (AGC, AGD), temperatures (40-70{\deg}C), and C-rates (C/20-1C). Remarkably, a single, consistent set of parameters is applied to simulate the capacity fade for all experiments without recalibration. While quantitative overestimations occur during high-SOC storage periods, the framework consistently captures the observed degradation trends. Our findings underscore that lower SOC operation mitigates degradation, establishing a physics-based model for predicting long-term lithium-ion battery aging.

papers.title: Mamba Quantum Eigensolver (MQE): A Selective State Space Model for Scalable Ground State Simulations in Quantum Chemistry
papers.summary: Predicting molecular electronic structure using Quantum Computing approaches is a challenge in Computational Chemistry. Traditional Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQEs) are typically hindered by optimization challenges. The alternative Generative Quantum Eigensolver (GQE) mitigates this by reformulating ground-state search as discrete sequence generation, but its Transformer backbone suffers from quadratic computational complexity, bottlenecking scalability for larger molecules. To address this, we introduce the Mamba Quantum Eigensolver (Mamba-QE), which replaces the Transformer with a Selective State Space Model (SSM) to process operator sequences with linear $\mathcal{O}(L)$ complexity. Additionally, we integrate a distance-conditioned mechanism enabling the direct prediction of complete potential energy surfaces (PES). Evaluated on the $H_2$ molecule, Mamba-QE reproduces Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) reference energies well within chemical accuracy, achieving an energy error below $3\times10^{-6}$ Ha across 16 geometries with zero variational violations. Mamba-QE maintains high expressive power while establishing a robust, scalable foundation for quantum simulations of complex molecular systems.

papers.title: Observation of Size-dependent Optical Modes and Confinement in Fin Cavities using Angle-Resolved Cathodoluminescence
papers.summary: We observe novel optical fringes and emission coherence in laterally formed semiconductor fins using wavelength- and angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (WARCL). These findings demonstrate that cavity mode and emission confinement are directly governed by cavity geometry including cavity dimensions, facet angles, and orientation. In flat fins narrowing the width from 3000 nm to 200 nm sharpens fringe intensity, indicating stronger mode confinement and increased coherence. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations confirm that the observed fringes originate from internal reflections among the fin facets, consistent with a Fabry-P\'erot (FP) cavity model where the cavity length determines the fringe spacing. FDTD also reveals a transition from multi-mode to single-longitudinal-mode behavior in 200-nm fins, consistent with experimentally observed fringe narrowing. Increasing fin length from 10 {\mu}m to 30 {\mu}m compresses fringe spacing via longer round-trip paths. Conversely, tilting the fin end-facet from 90{\deg} to 45{\deg} reduces the effective light path length, increasing the incoherent optical emission. Remarkably, this loss can be offset by adjusting the fin length-to-height ratio. Results suggest WARCL is a robust in-situ method for direct characterization of individual dielectric nanocavities, mapping their modal profiles and light directionality as a function of geometry for custom design of nanoscale optical sources and waveguides.

papers.title: Passive Phase-Aware Hadamard Decoding: Analytical and Machine-Learning Approaches
papers.summary: Hadamard-coded optical receivers typically rely on stable interference conditions, which can motivate active optical phase control. We investigate a fixed, intensity-only decoder that embeds four populated modes in an eight-mode interferometer and provides six complementary trigonometric observables through simultaneous power measurements. An analytic transition decoder uses the resulting sign-change patterns without continuous optical phase stabilization. The receiver's intensity-to-observable map is inverted exactly, and an identifiability analysis characterizes exceptional phase configurations and conditional noise sensitivity. An ideal, equal-photon-budget comparison with conventional four-port Hadamard decoding illustrates the potential value of the additional outputs without implying an unconditional advantage. Measurements on programmable photonic processors give 96.19% accuracy for the analytical decoding experiment; a complementary machine-learning analysis reports 98.31% on a held-out experimental trace. These results demonstrate an intensity-only, phase-aware approach to differential Hadamard decoding under the tested conditions, while larger codebooks and hardware-level energy benefits remain topics for future investigation.

papers.title: Teaching quantum mechanics in secondary schools: A qubit-first learning path to Bell's inequalities
papers.summary: Teaching quantum mechanics at the secondary school level remains a major educational challenge. Traditional historical approaches often present the theory as a sequence of disconnected phenomena, requiring extensive prior knowledge of classical physics before students can appreciate the conceptual structure of quantum physics. In this work, we present the design, implementation, and evaluation of a curriculum based on the two state (qubit first) approach, in which the fundamental postulates of quantum mechanics are introduced through mathematically accessible two level systems and realized with light polarization. The curriculum integrates theoretical instruction, laboratory activities, a coherent progression grounded in the interactive simulations, and inquiry based learning into a coherent pathway that progresses from quantum states and superposition to entanglement and the experimental violation of Bell's inequalities. A distinctive feature of the project is the experimental realization of the violation of Bell's inequalities obtained in a newly established quantum optics laboratory in an Italian high school, where students performed, for the first time in Italy, an authentic Bell test using polarization-entangled photons. The same educational framework was adopted for in service teacher professional development courses. Learning outcomes were evaluated through mixed methods. Preliminary analysis indicates significant improvements in conceptual understanding, confidence in using mathematical formalism, and appreciation of the relationship between theory, experimentation, and the foundations of quantum mechanics. The proposed curriculum shows that two-state formalism and supported by real laboratory experiences enables secondary-school students to engage more meaningfully with both the conceptual foundations of quantum mechanics and their experimental verification.

papers.title: Automated Discovery of Physically Interpretable Subgrid Length Scales for Detached Eddy Simulation via Agentic AI
papers.summary: Traditional turbulence-model development relies heavily on expert knowledge and is time-consuming. This study develops an agentic AI framework, DEScover (automated Discovery of DES closures), to explore subgrid length scales for detached eddy simulation (DES). The user provides only a modeling idea: the length scale is the grid width normal to the local vortex axis. Four large language model (LLM) agents then propose, review, implement, and evaluate candidate formulations and generate scripts for CFD simulations. The Discovery Agent infers the vortex axis from various vortex-identification methods. The candidates are tested on four cases spanning canonical and engineering flows: a flat plate, a backward-facing step, a free shear layer, and an iced airfoil. For all test cases, the best candidate consistently outperforms the standard length scale based on the maximum cell size. Its accuracy is similar to, or slightly better than, that of the expert-designed shear-layer-adapted length scale. Each agentic discovery run takes about 25 minutes on average, excluding the CFD simulations. These results show that LLM-based reasoning can significantly accelerate the discovery of physically interpretable turbulence models and reduce reliance on manual expert formulation.

papers.title: Differentiated Determinant Graphs Enable Large-Scale Multideterminant Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo
papers.summary: Multideterminant trial wave functions can reduce phaseless bias in auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC), but the repeated evaluation of their overlap, force bias, and local energy restricts systematic trial improvement. In this work, we organize particle--hole excitation determinants as a shared arithmetic directed acyclic graph of canonical minors. A coefficient-weighted reverse pass and batched directional passes evaluate the complete estimator without determinant-resolved cofactor tensors while preserving the sparse $\alpha$--$\beta$ coefficient coupling exactly. Controlled complex-valued tests verify the complete kernel to machine precision and show orders-of-magnitude acceleration over direct determinant summation. In molecular calculations, the observed cost remains sublinear through million-configuration selected-CI trials and the same estimator remains usable at one hundred million configurations, where the eventual exact coefficient-contraction boundary becomes visible. For Cr$_2$, an orbital-optimized CAS(12e,42o) trial in a double-$\zeta$ basis yields a potential-energy curve (PEC) and spectroscopic constants in close agreement with experiment. Differentiated determinant graphs therefore convert very large correlated trials from a formal accuracy hierarchy into a practical route for systematic AFQMC studies of strongly correlated molecules.

papers.title: Acoustic control of Rayleigh-regime liquid-jet breakup using a through-hole MHz transducer
papers.summary: This experimental study demonstrates MHz-order acoustic control of Rayleigh-regime liquid-jet breakup using a compact through-hole lithium niobate thickness-mode transducer integrated at the nozzle exit and driven near its 6.7 MHz resonance. Jet dynamics were measured by high-speed shadowgraphy at 50,000 fps, and breakup lengths were obtained from instantaneous jet-length records using an autocorrelation-based method that identifies statistically separated breakup events. Acoustic actuation produced visible interfacial corrugations and reduced the normalized breakup length, $L_b/d$, for both water and glycerol--water jets. In water, the response was threshold-like at low Weber number and weakened as the jet velocity increased to We ~ 50. A reduced-order threshold correlation, fit to the water amplitude and velocity sweeps, captured this abrupt shortening and the subsequent loss of actuation efficacy. More viscous glycerol--water mixtures shortened immediately at low forcing, indicating a distinct acoustic-coupling regime rather than a universal collapse of the water response. A wetting-control experiment showed that liquid spreading at the nozzle base can also shorten the jet, so the measured response reflects coupled radiation-pressure forcing, capillary-wave feedback, and wetting-mediated disturbance injection. Resolved droplet tracking further showed that MHz excitation changes the visible gate-crossing droplet population, although sub-resolution mist and micron-scale atomization were not measured. These results establish through-hole MHz actuation as a compact route for modifying free-surface jet breakup and provide a repeatable image-analysis protocol for experimental-fluid-mechanics measurements.

papers.title: Exact nonsymmetric vacuum magnetic field with nested toroidal flux surfaces and nonzero rotational transform
papers.summary: We show that an exact vacuum magnetic field without continuous Euclidean symmetry can fill a bounded solid torus with nested toroidal flux surfaces and nonzero rotational transform. We construct such a field in closed form and show that it is nowhere vanishing. Every off-axis field line closes after one toroidal transit and one poloidal turn, with rotational transform $\iota=-1$ on every flux surface. The solution provides an exact benchmark for three-dimensional equilibrium codes.

papers.title: Evaluation of Transverse Incoherent Tune Shifts in the Electron-Ion Collider
papers.summary: Achieving the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) peak luminosity goal of 10 to the power of 34 per square centimeter per second requires high average currents, flat beams, non-circular vacuum chambers, and large transverse orbit offsets in the Hadron Storage Ring (HSR) and Electron Storage Ring (ESR). These conditions can generate collective effects and incoherent tune spreads that drive particles across low-order betatron resonances, causing emittance growth, halo formation, and reduced beam lifetime. We quantitatively evaluate incoherent transverse betatron tune shifts from beam-beam interactions, direct space charge, and beam-environment interactions associated with image forces and vacuum chamber geometry. Xsuite and PyHEADTAIL simulations validate the analytical calculations for beam-beam and direct space-charge effects, respectively. For indirect space-charge effects, we review and compare several analytical formalisms and apply the Laslett image-charge formulation to rectangular vacuum chambers with off-axis beams. The analysis accounts for transverse orbit offsets of up to 20 mm in the HSR and 10 mm in the ESR. The results establish baseline parameters and provide quantitative guidance for EIC design, optimization, and operation. The comparison of indirect space-charge formalisms also offers an accessible reference and methodology for studies of high-intensity beam dynamics.

papers.title: NTL amplification in a SuperCDMS-style detector fabricated from a University of South Dakota-grown germanium crystal
papers.summary: Neganov-Trofimov-Luke (NTL) amplification enables eV-sub-keV detection thresholds for low-mass dark-matter and coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering experiments. We evaluated two University of South Dakota (USD)-grown germanium crystals fabricated as SuperCDMS-style four-channel athermal-phonon detectors and operated near 10 mK. The crystals had electrically active impurity concentrations near $10^10~\mathrm^-3$ and etch-pit densities of $300$-$7000~\mathrm^-2$. Contact-free biasing produced no resolvable amplification. However, after depositing a 600 nm aluminum bias contact, Detector~2 exhibited clear voltage-dependent NTL gain. The reconstructed channel-B energy increased from approximately 3.9 keV at 0 V to 34.9 keV at 40 V, corresponding to an 8.9-fold enhancement. Statistical centroid uncertainties were below 0.3%, while low-bias fits yielded effective prompt- and NTL-phonon response coefficients of $(6.77\pm0.82)%$ and $(4.77\pm0.20)%$, respectively, excluding systematic uncertainties. These results demonstrate the feasibility of USD-grown germanium for SuperCDMS-style high-voltage phonon detectors and highlight the importance of both crystal quality and contact fabrication in achieving NTL amplification.
