papers.title: Machine Learning-Enabled Wireless Power Transfer: A Task-Oriented Review of Structural Optimization, State and Parameter Estimation, and Adaptive Control
papers.summary: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems must maintain efficient and safe energy delivery under variations in geometry, coupling, load, alignment, and operating conditions. Machine-learning methods are increasingly applied to accelerate structural design, estimate operating parameters and states, and support adaptive control and scheduling. This review develops a task-oriented framework organized around three interconnected domains: structural design and optimization, parameter and state estimation, and control and optimization. Supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and hybrid or physics-informed methods are compared in terms of data requirements, dependence on physical models, information sources, computational requirements, accuracy, online response, application scope, and optimization objectives. Supervised learning provides rapid surrogate modeling, regression, and classification when representative labeled data are available. Reinforcement learning addresses sequential control and scheduling but introduces challenges in reward design, safe exploration, and simulation-to-reality transfer. Hybrid methods integrate physical knowledge with data-driven models to improve data efficiency and physical consistency. The principal barriers to engineering deployment include limited and biased datasets, weak out-of-distribution generalization, insufficient physical consistency, unsafe online adaptation, embedded-resource constraints, and the absence of standardized benchmarks. Future research should prioritize uncertainty-aware and physics-informed learning, safe simulation-to-reality transfer, lightweight edge deployment, distributed coordination, reproducible evaluation, and digital-twin-assisted development.

papers.title: Implementation of Dynamic Microsegmentation for a Multi-Robot Network
papers.summary: This report describes a laboratory instantiation of a dynamic microsegmentation function for an Internet-of-Things network, specifically a multi-robot network, using a commercial software-defined microsegmentation tool. Fine-grained dynamic segmentation policies are defined, where segments are adapted based on asset functional and health tags. Automated implementation of the dynamic policies in software is also undertaken. The microsegmentation solution is shown to automatically isolate an indicated threat in real time, while maintaining unaffected operations. The demonstration indicates that microsegmentation can be implemented in IoT networks, in a way that allows for robust operation in the face of threats and disruptions.

papers.title: Geometric Algebra for Neural Networks: A Survey
papers.summary: Geometric algebra (GA) unifies geometric primitives and transformations in a single algebraic framework. Neural networks designed around this framework often represent features as multivectors and constrain layer operations to respect the algebraic structure, enabling principled treatment of geometric transformations and, in many cases, built-in equivariance. This survey reviews geometric algebra neural networks, including their building blocks, equivariant properties, application domains, empirical performance, and software support. We provide an algebra-selection guide, an empirical comparison of GA-based and other equivariant architectures, and a failure-mode analysis covering training pathologies, deployment constraints, and performance limitations. Across the surveyed literature, the strongest evidence for GA-based architectures appears in settings with explicit geometric symmetries and heterogeneous geometric entities; evidence for broader advantages in parameter efficiency, interpretability, and dense prediction is comparatively limited and uneven. We therefore conclude that geometric algebra neural networks are not universally superior to well-tuned non-GA equivariant baselines, and outline open problems in algebra selection, numerical stability, scalable implementation, and reproducible evaluation.

papers.title: DeGroot Dynamics on Multiplex Networks with Directed and Acyclic Interlayer Connectivities
papers.summary: In models of opinion dynamics, researchers typically examine how an individual's opinion on one topic is influenced by the opinions of their neighbors in a network. However, people's opinions on a topic are also influenced by their opinions and their neighbors' opinions on related topics. In an election, for example, the opinions of a voter on a variety of issues inform their opinions of electoral candidates. To consider the influence between people's opinions on multiple distinct topics, we study a multiplex extension of the traditional DeGroot consensus model. In our multiplex DeGroot model, different network layers represent distinct topics and directed interlayer edges (which are not allowed to form cycles) encode relationships between distinct topics. In our model, an individual's opinion on one topic is influenced both by the opinions of their neighbors on that topic and by their own opinions on related topics. We prove under mild conditions that our multiplex DeGroot model converges to a limit state. We also prove that strong connectedness in ``source layers'' (which represent fundamental beliefs) eventually yields a consensus opinion in each layer. In particular, we show that consensus on source layers can lead to consensus on other layers even when those layers otherwise would be polarized. By numerically simulating our multiplex DeGroot model on a two-layer network, we examine the effects on opinion dynamics of (1) different network structures and (2) different types of initial opinion data.

papers.title: Optimal R\'enyi and Logarithmic Additive Functional Entropy Estimation
papers.summary: We characterize the minimax sample complexity of estimating R\'enyi entropy from independent samples on an alphabet of size at most $k$, when the known order $\alpha>1$ may vary with $k$. For every fixed additive accuracy $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ and success probability $2/3$, we prove matching bounds with constants independent of $k$ and $\alpha$. For $10$ for $x>0$, and $f(x)\sim ax^r$ at zero, with $a>0$ and $r>1$, estimating $-\beta^{-1}\log\sum_i f(p_i)$ at fixed accuracy, for fixed $\beta>0$, has sample complexity $\Theta(k^{1-1/r})$ for integer $r$ and $\Theta(k/\log k)$ otherwise. A replication reduction preserves the sampling experiment and transfers the rates for powers. Smooth flat functions show that regularity alone does not determine the complexity. The upper bound combines polynomial approximation, Gamma count statistics, and an independent pilot, with a global affine correction near order one. The lower bound uses interpolation to construct positive mean-one priors and controls their distinguishability and entropy separation after normalization. Exact count-variance identities and weighted approximation duality connect the two arguments.

papers.title: KunSet: A Corpus and Benchmark for Lyrics Alignment and Rhyme Retrieval in Kunqu Opera
papers.summary: Kunqu is one of the oldest extant forms of Chinese opera, yet its digitization remains scarce and difficult to annotate, with two challenges standing out: first, close analysis of Kunqu performance demands syllable-level lyrics alignment; second, analyzing Kunqu pronunciation requires its phonological attributes (e.g., rhyme) to be linked with each syllable. To address these challenges, we present KunSet, the first Kunqu performance corpus comprising 482,164 fine-grained annotations of syllable-level lyrics and phonological attributes in total media duration of 155.2 h with 106.3 h annotated. To ensure annotation quality, KunSet was preannotated by an iterative ML-assisted pipeline and corrected by over 200 trained annotators via a purpose-built online annotation system under a two-round review process. To assess KunSet as a music information retrieval (MIR) benchmark, we evaluate two tasks: lyrics alignment, by finetuning a forced-alignment model with an acoustic anchor decoder; and same-rhyme retrieval, using frozen Chinese HuBERT features. Models built with KunSet outperform their baselines. We release KunSet and model checkpoints to support MIR research on traditional-music corpora.

papers.title: Payload generalization on feedforward control actions for trajectory tracking in robots with rigid and elastic joints
papers.summary: Industries employ robots for repetitive tasks due to their high precision and performance, typically achieved through feedforward control actions based on an accurate robot description. However, an exact dynamic model can be difficult to obtain, especially for robots with elastic elements or when the payload changes. Learning-based feedforward approaches are promising for trajectory tracking under model uncertainties, but typically face generalization issues when task parameters vary. This paper proposes a novel method to generalize the feedforward control action with respect to payload parameters, independently of the underlying controller. Firstly, the minimal number of example objects needed for payload generalization is derived. Then, an algorithm is proposed to execute the same trajectory with a new payload, given only its parameters, without knowledge of the robot's dynamic model and even in the presence of elastic joints. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is validated in simulations and experiments on tracking tasks with different robots and controllers. Two sets of experiments are performed: on a standard Franka Emika Panda robot, and on a Franka Emika Panda robot equipped with an elastic wrist.

papers.title: Integrating Flow Matching and Model Predictive Control for Safe Robot Navigation
papers.summary: Learning-based path planners based on diffusion and flow matching can generate diverse trajectories from demonstrations but typically lack mechanisms for constraint satisfaction and collision avoidance during deployment. This work proposes a framework that combines flow-matching-based path planning with model predictive path-following control to integrate data-driven path generation with real-time, constraint-aware execution. The flow-matching model captures multimodal path distributions, while the predictive controller adapts motion online to satisfy state and input constraints and avoid obstacles using updated local sensor information. An event-triggered re-planning scheme incorporates predictive control solutions into subsequent path generation, promoting collision-free navigation in environments with previously unseen obstacles. Simulation results for mobile robot navigation demonstrate robust performance across cluttered environments. The framework provides a systematic approach to combining flow matching with predictive control for adaptive, data-driven navigation.

papers.title: RubatoCodec: Budgeted Adaptive Speech Tokenization with Streaming Decoding
papers.summary: Neural speech codecs provide discrete tokens for speech generation. Lower frame rates shorten token sequences, but each token must then carry more linguistic and acoustic information. Variable-frame-rate codecs address this trade-off by adapting token allocation to speech content, but threshold-based allocation lets content determine the token count, so the sequence length a speech generator must produce varies across utterances and datasets at a fixed setting. We present RubatoCodec, a variable-frame-rate speech codec built on X-Codec-2 with an exact utterance-level event budget and streaming decoding. Its Adaptive Firing mechanism uses changes in codec features and waveform spectra to divide speech into variable-duration events without a learned boundary predictor. Discrete codes and an explicit duration represent each event, allowing a speech generator to predict and decode one event at a time. Controlled experiments show that adaptive allocation outperforms fixed-rate coding in reconstruction fidelity and intelligibility at low event rates. A model trained on large-scale multilingual speech achieves competitive reconstruction quality across English, Japanese, and Mandarin, with the best intelligibility preservation among the compared codecs on the evaluated English and Japanese benchmarks at comparable bitrates. In a matched text-to-speech comparison, the adaptive representation yields lower WER and higher UTMOS and UTMOSv2 with comparable speaker similarity. The speech generator also learns the codec's utterance-level event budget without an explicit generation-time rate constraint. These results demonstrate that budgeted adaptive speech representations support both high-quality reconstruction and streaming text-to-speech generation. Code and weights are available at https://github.com/third-intelligence/RubatoCodec and https://huggingface.co/third-intelligence/RubatoCodec.

papers.title: Approximate Matrix Multiplication through Joint Leverage Score Sampling
papers.summary: In this paper, we investigate approximate matrix multiplication through random sampling. We provide the probability error bounds for the proposed algorithm are also given, and discuss connections to data-oblivious approximate matrix multiplication, and graph sparsification algorithms.

papers.title: Point Cloud Transmission With Patch-Based Rate Adaptation
papers.summary: We propose a joint source-channel coding (JSCC) framework for efficient wireless point cloud transmission. In the proposed scheme, the point cloud is first divided into local patches and transformed into compact latent representations, which are then mapped to symbols for transmission over a noisy channel. Our model incorporates an entropy model that exploits inter-patch spatial dependencies to estimate patch-level coding costs and allocate different numbers of symbols accordingly. Unlike existing patch-based point cloud JSCC methods that use the same transmission rate between patches, we adapt the channel usage of each patch latent representation. To exploit inter-patch dependencies without patch-by-patch autoregressive processing, we select a group of anchor patches whose features provide contextual information for entropy estimation of non-anchor ones. The framework is trained using a reconstruction loss and an entropy-based rate surrogate. Experiments on ModelNet40 demonstrate overall rate-distortion improvements over existing baselines across channel conditions.

papers.title: S-PASS: Star-Topology Pinching-Antenna Systems with Pipelined Antenna Pre-Positioning
papers.summary: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) flexibly reconfigure the wireless channel by positioning dielectric antennas along a waveguide near each user. Releasing and re-attaching an antenna, however, is a mechanical operation orders of magnitude slower than electronic switching, wasting much transmission time. Existing designs generally assume instant reconfiguration, neglect the mechanical latency, or keep the antenna fixed. This paper proposes S-PASS, a star architecture of waveguides sharing one radio-frequency chain through a switch, and pipelined antenna pre-positioning (PAP), a time-division protocol in which idle waveguides pre-position their antennas for their next users while one transmits. It derives in closed form the scheduling efficiency, the number of waveguides beyond which the latency costs no transmission time, and the latency up to which PAP outperforms fixed placement. Analytical and numerical results show that this latency grows with each added waveguide, and users at the outer ends of the waveguides gain most.

papers.title: Worst-Case Finite-Horizon Analysis of Perturbed LQR via Performance Estimation Problem
papers.summary: We propose an exact formulation to quantify the finite-horizon robustness of a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) subject to norm-bounded Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) parametric uncertainties, using the Performance Estimation Problem (PEP) framework. Originally developed for optimization, this method allows us to reformulate the worst-case performance search as a rank-constrained Semidefinite Program (SDP). By applying operator interpolation, this formulation retains the sequence variables, allowing the worst-case to be explicitly reconstructed when a rank-one solution is found. This approach also opens new possibilities for the finite-horizon certification of broader system classes, such as data-driven models or nonlinear components. Using this framework, we observe that finite-horizon LTI perturbations do not simply follow asymptotic strategies. Instead, they align slowly decaying invariant manifolds with specific initial conditions to drive transient growth, causing a bifurcation in the worst-case behavior as the horizon length changes. Finally, we show numerically that our performance bounds sit between the upper bounds of Integral Quadratic Constraint (IQC) relaxations and a lower bound derived from a pseudospectral heuristic.

papers.title: A Learned Musical-Time Coordinate for Piano Audio-to-Score Transcription
papers.summary: End-to-end piano audio-to-score (A2S) transcription is the task of reconstructing a notated score from an audio recording in a single system. Existing A2S approaches usually rely on pre-segmented excerpts, and few handle whole pieces without external segmentation. This raises the question of whether a musical-time coordinate can guide score transcription while also helping the system segment whole pieces. Previous work on jazz saxophone A2S uses an external beat tracker to obtain such a coordinate for score prediction. We introduce downbeat phase, a musical-time coordinate learned jointly with score transcription that represents each audio frame's relative position within a notated bar. With this coordinate, our system can not only condition its score decoder on downbeat phase but also self-segment at bar boundaries and stitch the segments into a whole piece. Evaluation suggests that the coordinate improves metrical structure and supports whole-piece transcription with comparable notation quality.

papers.title: Enhancing IoT Network Reliability through Antenna Diversity in Real-World Scenarios
papers.summary: Antenna diversity in Internet of Things (IoT) devices is explored to address challenges associated with fixed device orientation and interference from nearby metallic objects, which can degrade wireless network performance. These findings suggest that the added complexity in hardware and software to incorporate antenna diversity could well be justified by the resulting enhancements in network stability for real-world applications.

papers.title: Dual Effect and Certainty Equivalence Revisited for a Linear-Gaussian Dual Control Problem
papers.summary: This paper revisits the relation between dual effect and certainty equivalence (CE) through a scalar linear-Gaussian model. In dual control, the current input affects not only the immediate cost but also the information available for future decisions, and hence the future cost. Dynamic programming (DP) provides a natural framework for formulating dual control problems. At each step of the Bellman recursion, an optimal input minimizes the sum of the stage cost and the expected cost-to-go. We restrict attention to stage costs minimized by the CE input. However, CE may not minimize the Bellman objective because of the input-dependent expected cost-to-go. Classical no-dualeffect (NDE) conditions guarantee CE optimality in certain problem classes by requiring the conditional distribution of the estimation error to be independent of past controls. In the present model, we observe that CE can remain optimal at the level of a single Bellman recursion even when the classical NDE conditions fail, provided that the expected cost-to-go is independent of the current input. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a notion of NDE formulated directly at the level of the Bellman objective, which we call Bellman-side NDE. Under some mild regularity conditions, we show that Bellman-side NDE can be characterized by a heat equation. This characterization identifies the class of Bellman-side NDE functions, and further yields a decomposition of a generic cost-to-go function into a Bellman-side NDE component and a dual-effect component.

papers.title: Distributed Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming for Mixed-Traffic Intersection Control
papers.summary: In this paper, we develop a distributed solution framework for coordinating traffic light systems and connected automated vehicles (CAVs) in mixed-traffic intersections. We formulate a mixed-integer quadratic program (MIQP) aimed at optimizing the coordination of traffic light systems and CAVs, thereby fully capitalizing on the advantages of CAV integration under conditions of high penetration rates. To effectively solve the challenging multi-agent MIQP approximately, we employ proximal ADMM for solving the convex relaxation of the MIQP while systematically tightening the constraint coefficients using a finite-grid tightening rule to uphold integrality requirements. \hilitediff{The obtained relaxed solutions are corrected using a confidence-guided binary recovery step, which fixes high-confidence binary variables and solves a substantially reduced MIQP over the remaining uncertain binaries to improve the feasibility of the final mixed-integer solution.} The performance of our control framework and the efficacy of the distributed algorithm are rigorously validated through a series of simulations conducted across varying penetration rates and traffic volumes.

papers.title: Stochastic Neural Control Barrier Functions
papers.summary: Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) are utilized to ensure the safety of control systems. CBFs act as safety filters in order to provide safety guarantees without compromising system performance. These safety guarantees rely on the construction of valid CBFs. Due to their complexity, CBFs can be represented by neural networks, known as neural CBFs (NCBFs). Existing works on the verification of the NCBF focus on the synthesis and verification of NCBFs in deterministic settings, leaving the stochastic NCBFs (SNCBFs) less studied. In this work, we propose a verifiably safe synthesis for SNCBFs. We consider the cases of smooth SNCBFs with twice-differentiable activation functions and SNCBFs that utilize the Rectified Linear Unit or ReLU activation function. We propose a verification-free synthesis framework for smooth SNCBFs and a verification-in-the-loop synthesis framework for both smooth and ReLU SNCBFs. and we validate our frameworks in three cases, namely, the inverted pendulum, Darboux, and the unicycle model.

papers.title: Towards channel foundation models (CFMs): Motivations, methodologies and opportunities
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) models for wireless systems are commonly optimized for fixed tasks, channel distributions, and system configurations, which limits their reuse when downstream objectives or operating conditions change. Channel foundation models (CFMs) address this limitation by pretraining reusable models on channel-informative observations and adapting their parameters or representations across channel-related tasks and conditions. However, existing studies differ substantially in their input modalities, pretraining targets, retained components, and transfer settings, making it difficult to compare how the methods are constructed, reused, and evaluated. This paper surveys CFM research through the central question of how channel-informative pretraining is converted into reusable downstream capabilities. We adopt a channel-centered scope covering explicit channel state information, received-signal observations, and auxiliary environmental or geometric context. Existing methods are organized according to the source of their learning targets into observation-space modeling, relational representation learning, latent-space prediction, task-target learning, system-utility optimization, and hybrid combinations. For representative methods, we compare how reusable parameters are learned and adapted, their downstream applications, and the settings used to evaluate transfer. The resulting framework connects CFM methodologies to physical-layer processing, radio access network and medium access control tasks, integrated sensing and communication, and radio-environment modeling. A matched case study further compares transfer for channel extrapolation, beam prediction, and positioning under common backbone and source-data settings. Finally, we discuss open problems in data construction, transfer evaluation, efficient adaptation, deployment, reliability, privacy, and security.

papers.title: Optimal Control of Behavioral-Feedback SIR Epidemic Model
papers.summary: We consider a behavioral-feedback SIR epidemic model, in which the infection rate depends in feedback on the fractions of susceptible and infected agents. Contrary to the classic SIR dynamics, the considered model allows one to account for endogenous adaptation mechanisms of the agents in response to the epidemics, such as voluntary social distancing, or the adoption of face masks. For this model, we formulate an optimal control problem for a social planner that has the ability to reduce the infection rate to keep the infection curve below a certain threshold within an infinite time horizon, while minimizing the intervention cost. Based on the dynamic properties of the model, we prove that, under quite general conditions on the infection rate, the filling-the-box strategy is the optimal control. This strategy consists in letting the epidemics spread without intervention until the threshold is reached, then applying the minimum control that leaves the fraction of infected individuals constantly at the threshold until the reproduction number becomes less than one and the infection naturally fades out. Our contribution enhances the understanding of epidemic management while accounting for adaptive human behavior, offering novel insights for robust containment strategies.

papers.title: A Semi-spontaneous Dutch Speech Dataset for Speech Enhancement and Speech Recognition
papers.summary: We present DRES: a 1.5-hour Dutch realistic elicited (semi-spontaneous) speech dataset from 80 speakers recorded in noisy, public indoor environments. DRES was designed as a test set for the evaluation of state-of-the-art (SotA) automatic speech recognition (ASR) and speech enhancement (SE) models in a real-world scenario: a person speaking in a public indoor space with background talkers and noise. The speech was recorded with a four-channel linear microphone array. In this work we evaluate the speech quality of five well-known single-channel SE algorithms and the recognition performance of eight SotA off-the-shelf ASR models before and after applying SE on the speech of DRES. We found that five out of the eight ASR models have WERs lower than 22\% on DRES, despite the challenging conditions. In contrast to recent work, we did not find a positive effect of modern single-channel SE on ASR performance, emphasizing the importance of evaluating in realistic conditions.

papers.title: Region of Attraction Estimation for Linear Quadratic Regulator, Linear and Robust Model Predictive Control on a Two-Wheeled Inverted Pendulum
papers.summary: Nonlinear underactuated systems such as two-wheeled inverted pendulums (TWIPs) exhibit a limited region of attraction (RoA), which defines the set of initial conditions from which the closed-loop system converges to the equilibrium. The RoA of nonlinear and constrained systems is generally nonconvex and analytically intractable, requiring numerical or approximate estimation methods. This work investigates the estimation of the RoA for a TWIP stabilized under three model-based control strategies: saturated linear quadratic regulator (LQR), linear model predictive control (MPC), and constraint tightening MPC (CTMPC). We first derive a Lyapunov-based invariant set that provides a certified inner approximation of the RoA. Since this analytical bound is highly conservative, a Monte Carlo-based estimation procedure is then employed to obtain a more representative approximation of the RoA, capturing how the controllers behave beyond the analytically guaranteed region. The proposed methodology combines analytical guarantees with data-driven estimation, providing both a formally certified inner bound and an empirical characterization of the RoA, offering a practical way to evaluate controller performance without relying solely on conservative analytical bounds or purely empirical simulation.

papers.title: ACHEM: A Real-Time Digital Twin Framework with Channel and Radio Emulation
papers.summary: Digital twins are becoming an important tool for designing, developing, testing, and optimizing next-generation wireless communication systems. Over the past decade, system softwarization has become a reality, and wireless communication systems are no exception. Software-Defined Radios (SDRs), in general, and Universal Software Radio Peripherals (USRPs), in particular, are often used for prototyping and testing advanced wireless systems. Unfortunately, there is currently no end-to-end, software-based, general-purpose testing environment for SDR-based systems: developers often rely on benchtop setups or even small testbeds, but those are costly and cumbersome to build. At the other end of the spectrum, simulations often rely on simplified channel/radio models and typically do not execute full-stack production code, which can increase development effort and reduce fidelity. In this paper, we propose ACHEM (A Channel Emulator), the first software-based, end-to-end wireless channel emulation environment and toolset for communication systems based on SDRs, specifically USRPs. With the proposed emulator and toolkit, any USRP-based system can be fully emulated at the I/Q level in a pure digital environment without requiring specialized hardware (e.g., vehicles, USRPs, FPGAs, or GPUs). The proposed emulator supports multiple transmitters and receivers, MIMO communications, multiple frequencies, heterogeneous sampling rates, real-time node mobility through vehicle emulation, antenna radiation patterns, and various channel models. ACHEM facilitates wireless digital twin development and deployment. ACHEM is validated with several popular open-source USRP-based wireless communication applications, including GNU Radio, srsRAN 4G/5G, and OpenAirInterface.

papers.title: The Cheap Hours Don't Stay Cheap: Price-Chasing Data Centers Reshape Grids and Markets
papers.summary: Data centers unsettle the paradigm of location-bound electricity demand: computing workloads can migrate across sites and hours, whereas facilities and grid connections remain fixed. This mobility reduces electricity costs but reshapes the spatiotemporal structure of nodal prices. A model-driven framework couples US wholesale market signals with optimal fleet scheduling, showing how their interaction alters prices and other participants' responses. Greater flexibility enlarges savings yet can erode network benefits: in a Texas study, temporal shifting and cross-site allocation each relieve congestion, but their combination leaves total congestion nearly unchanged. At continental scale, computing demand gravitating toward cheaper electricity narrows price differences and compresses the low-price hours storage arbitrage relies on, threatening storage investment recovery. Cost-minimizing scheduling may therefore undermine grid-supporting resources. Comparing job-level and aggregate fleet representations reveals a trade-off between operational visibility and information disclosure, informing requirements and incentives that could turn workload mobility into a lever for system-wide efficiency.

papers.title: Unsupervised Learning for Scalable Downlink Power Control in Cell-Free Massive MIMO
papers.summary: In cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output systems, downlink power control is essential to ensure uniformly high service quality across users. Existing solutions range from computationally demanding centralized optimization to scalable distributed schemes with limited fairness. This letter proposes an unsupervised, physics-informed framework that directly optimizes max-min fairness without optimal labels or user position information. The method scales with the number of UEs, requires no retraining when the number of UEs changes, and admits a fully scalable extension. Numerical results show that it nearly doubles the worst-user spectral efficiency over existing scalable schemes.

papers.title: Foundation Models for Wireless Communications: From PHY Intelligence to Network Autonomy
papers.summary: 6G networks will introduce unprecedented complexity, which calls for a paradigm shift in network optimization and management. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based solutions, especially those enabled by the recently developed foundation models, have been recognized as promising candidates. Foundation models are large-scale AI models with general-purpose feature extraction capabilities, and once trained on massive amounts of data, they can be adapted to solve a wide range of downstream tasks, either in a zero-shot manner or with few-shot fine-tuning. This article provides a comprehensive overview of how foundation models are reshaping physical-layer processing and wireless resource management across three progressive paradigms. First, we examine the adaptation of off-the-shelf pre-trained foundation models to various wireless tasks. Second, we explore wireless-native foundation models, built from scratch on wireless data to bridge cross-domain modality gaps and capture universal wireless-domain physical characteristics. Third, we highlight agentic foundation models, which elevate static data processing into autonomous, reasoning-driven network orchestration. Furthermore, we discuss the impact of applying foundation models to emerging 6G frontiers, including integrated sensing and communications (ISAC), new multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architectures, semantic communications, and system-level network autonomy. Finally, we identify critical open challenges and opportunities, charting a promising path toward fully intelligent and adaptive wireless networks.

papers.title: Evaluating Grid Resilience in the Era of Ever-Increasing Data Centers
papers.summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence workloads is increasing the scale and concentration of data center demand, creating new concerns for power system resilience under disruptive events. This paper extends a validated multi-time-step DC optimal power flow framework to evaluate the impact of aggregated data center demand on contingency-induced unserved energy. Using an IEEE 30-bus system with flexible resources, we replace a conventional load at a contingency-exposed bus with an energy-matched constant data center load and examine two capacity-growth levels under generator derating, transmission line derating, and coupled derating. The results show that data center capacity growth substantially increases both system-level and data-center-bus unserved energy under transmission-constrained contingencies. Under coupled derating, the high-growth case increases total unserved energy from 3.203 MWh in the energy-matched case to 22.891 MWh. A supplementary energy-matched coincident-demand case further increases total unserved energy by 34.4%, indicating that temporally concentrated data center demand can amplify resilience impacts even without increasing total energy consumption.

papers.title: Fast Cascaded Recursive Filtering via a Block-Matrix Reformulation
papers.summary: Recursive (IIR) filters realized as cascaded second-order sections (biquads) offer both design generality and robustness against coefficient quantization. However, their inherent sample-to-sample feedback dependency poses a fundamental obstacle to parallel computation. This paper reformulates the biquad difference equation as a banded block-Toeplitz linear system. It relies on a stride-$N$ permutation that maps a group of $NL$ samples into a block-tridiagonal structure whose entries are scalar multiples of identity and shift matrices. Within this framework, two data-parallel algorithms are developed which, to the best of our knowledge, are the fastest, single-core IIR filter implementations reported to date. A partial LU (PH) factorization preserves the sparse block structure and a cyclic reduction reduces the sequential dependency depth from $\mathcal{O}(N)$ to $\mathcal{O}(\log_2 N)$. For a cascade of $K$ biquads, the intermediate permutations between successive sections cancel exactly, so that only a single pair of permutations is required for the entire cascade. Exact block-level operation counts are derived for every algorithmic stage and validated against cycle-accurate measurements on three micro-architectures supporting AVX2 SIMD instructions. Experimental results for a 16th-order system show that the proposed multi-block algorithms reduce clock cycles per sample by up to $10\times$ compared to scalar filtering, with both algorithms scaling favorably on newer architectures. On a single Meteor Lake core, cyclic reduction achieves approximately 616 MS/s---four times the throughput of Intel's vendor-tuned IPP library.

papers.title: Computational and Effective Degrees of Freedom for Spatially Stationary HMIMO Channel Modeling
papers.summary: This paper establishes a comprehensive theoretical framework for the continuous-to-discrete modeling of spatially stationary holographic MIMO (HMIMO) channels utilizing the Nystrom method with Gauss-Legendre quadrature (NGLQ). Starting with an operator-theoretic analysis of the NGLQ method, we prove that its quadrature error exhibits a super-exponential decay. Furthermore, we derive a spatial sampling threshold, termed computational degrees of freedom (cDoF), which reveals a {\pi}/2 oversampling penalty over the physical DoF for 1D arrays, compounding to a 68% computational redundancy for 2D separable grids. To address the ill-conditioning of the eigenvalue decomposition (EVD) problem inherent to the Nystrom discretization, we invoke the multidimensional Szego-Widom asymptotic expansion. This analysis yields a physically grounded semi-analytical expression for the effective DoF (eDoF) of 2D rectangular apertures, capturing the anisotropic boundary truncation effects to guide partial EVD and reduce computational complexity. Numerical evaluations confirm the tightness of the cDoF threshold under worst-case end-fire conditions. Moreover, simulations utilizing closed-form kernels for isotropic scattering verify that the derived eDoF acts as an accurate asymptotic approximation. Finally, by deploying the exact non-uniform discrete Fourier transform to eliminate interpolation error floors, we demonstrate spectral convergence down to the machine-precision level for non-isotropic scattering environments.

papers.title: Analytical Prediction of Equilibrium Existence in Current-Limited Grid-Forming Inverters
papers.summary: As converter-interfaced units become dominant in power systems, understanding nonlinear stability phenomena involving discrete switching events becomes essential for secure operation. The limited overcurrent capability of grid-forming (GFM) inverters makes current limiting essential during large disturbances. Activation of a circular current limiter (CCL) can cause the operating equilibrium to disappear under certain circumstances. This paper develops an analytical framework to predict the grid-voltage boundaries for CCL activation and determine whether the operating equilibrium persists or disappears after activation. For CCL-based GFM inverters with frozen anti-windup, closed-form expressions for the activation boundaries are derived while accounting for the filter capacitor. A criterion is established to determine whether a saturated (i.e., current-limited) stable equilibrium point (satSEP) persists following limiter activation. A continuation method is also developed to trace equilibria across normal-control and current-limited operation. Power-angle analysis and dynamic-model continuation in single-inverter and modified 9-bus systems validate these predictions. Time-domain simulations further confirm the results. The results show that CCL activation can either cause immediate loss of the stable equilibrium or allow stable current-limited operation to continue until the equilibrium is lost as operating conditions change further.

papers.title: Depth through recurrence: Looped transformers for flow-matching TTS
papers.summary: We study how to organize Transformer depth through recurrence in flow-matching text-to-speech, varying the amount, order, and placement of weight reuse. Seven layouts perform 18 block calls per network evaluation under a common training objective and sampler. On Seed-TTS and LibriSpeech-PC, SEQUENCE applies each of nine blocks twice consecutively, retaining competitive intelligibility, speaker similarity, and predicted speech quality at 32 sampling steps with 47.1% fewer parameters than the unshared baseline. Cycling six blocks three times further reduces model size but raises 32-step word error rates relative to cycling nine blocks twice. At matched parameter counts and executed depth, reuse order and sharing position produce different quality trade-offs. These comparisons depend on sampling budget: Prefix and Suffix have similar 32-step word error rates, but Suffix is worse by 3.44 and 5.97 percentage points at four steps on the two datasets, respectively. Only Middle ranks first or second in mean word error rate at 32 and four steps on both datasets. These results show that the organization of recurrent computation affects synthesis quality, and that reuse layouts should be selected for both the sampling budget and the quality dimensions of interest.

papers.title: Traffic State Prediction and Control Using a Koopman Operator Framework with Polynomial Observables
papers.summary: In this paper, we develop a Koopman operator framework for modeling and control of traffic flow governed by the Lighthill--Whitham--Richards (LWR) conservation law. We show that the nonlinear dynamics induced by the Greenshields flow--density relation naturally motivate a dictionary of polynomial observables, while the controlled dynamics become bilinear in the lifted Koopman coordinates. A reduced-order Koopman model is identified from spatio-temporal traffic-density snapshots and used as the prediction model in a model predictive control (MPC) framework for ramp metering. The resulting Koopman-MPC is compared with two predictive control baselines that use, respectively, a fixed linearized LWR model and the nonlinear finite-volume LWR model. In a one-hour freeway experiment, the Koopman-based controller maintains the traffic density below the critical Greenshields value and closely reproduces the behavior of the nonlinear PDE-based MPC, with a maximum-density difference below 1%. The Koopman predictor also reduces the mean online model-evaluation cost by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the nonlinear PDE predictor. In contrast, the linearized LWR predictor is computationally cheaper but exhibits substantially larger prediction errors and yields a more conservative metering policy. These results demonstrate that the analytical structure of the nonlinear traffic conservation law can be exploited to construct an interpretable data-driven surrogate for efficient traffic prediction and control

papers.title: Physics-Informed Koopman Learning for Data-Efficient System Identification of Automated Vehicle Dynamics
papers.summary: Understanding how a particular automated vehicle reacts to nearby traffic can improve motion prediction, control development, traffic simulation, and safety evaluation. However, commercial automated driving systems are proprietary, and single encounters may provide only a few seconds of noisy data. Standard physical models are interpretable but inflexible, whereas neural models are often data-hungry. We propose a physics-informed Koopman framework that combines a calibrated car-following law with a correction learned from the observations. A weak-form estimator learns this correction from velocity measurements integrated over time, avoiding noise-sensitive numerical differentiation. The resulting continuous-time model predicts the follower's response and provides interpretable measures of driving behavior. Experiments on OpenACC and CATS-CF evaluate 5-, 7-, and 11-second histories. Averaged over these histories, the constant-time-headway branch reduces speed prediction error by 16.0% and 15.4% on OpenACC and CATS-CF, respectively, relative to the best neural baselines. The PI-Koopman branches achieve the lowest mean speed and gap errors among the physical and neural comparators. Weak-form estimation reduces acceleration-field reconstruction error by 74.5% in noisy known-law simulations and noise-induced field perturbation by 91.6% in paired real-vehicle measurements. The same PI-Koopman system identification supports following-mode recognition with an approximately eleven-fold difference in median residual variance between human drivers and automated vehicles, and a single residual threshold achieves 85.4% balanced accuracy. The branch informed by the intelligent driver model takes a median 17 to 26 ms for identification and forecasting on the tested central processing units, supporting frequent target adaptation.

papers.title: Latency-Neutral Passive Cyber Monitoring for Grid-Edge Operational Technology Networks
papers.summary: Deterministic industrial networks often present an operational trade-off between maintaining microsecond timing of primary control loops and capturing security telemetry. This work investigates the engineering feasibility of the Operational Technology Supervisor (OTSV), a three-tier passive monitoring framework designed to resolve this visibility challenge within timing-sensitive grid-edge infrastructure. By utilizing a Layer-3-unconfigured passive ingestion mode on bare-metal hardware via a physical switched port analyzer (SPAN) loop, the deep packet inspection engine is isolated from the production network, implementing a software-enforced unidirectional export policy. Performance validation conducted over a continuous audit comprising 32,927 active-monitoring round-trip time (RTT) samples yielded stable latency distributions across a laboratory power-monitoring loop running Modbus TCP and IEC 61850 MMS protocols. The measured latency delta between the unmonitored baseline and the active monitoring state was less than 0.12 milliseconds, supporting the feasibility of continuous high-fidelity security observation alongside stringent grid-edge metering timing bounds without measurably degrading the monitored reporting path.

papers.title: A Hierarchical Space-Ground Collaborative Network: Architecture Design and Deployment
papers.summary: The sixth-generation (6G) landscape demands a profound architectural evolution toward a unified, collaborative ecosystem that integrates satellite and terrestrial segments to provide ubiquitous global connectivity. Nevertheless, conventional independent management paradigms are increasingly challenged by the profound spatiotemporal nonstationarity of low-Earth orbit (LEO) channels and the volatile demands of massive heterogeneous services. To address these challenges, this study focuses on the architectural design of space-ground integrated networks (SGINs) and investigates elastic deployment strategies tailored to heterogeneous 6G service requirements. We first review the development trends in SGIN and then summarize typical application scenarios into two categories, along with their associated challenges and constraints. After that, a hierarchical space-ground collaborative network (SGCN) architecture is proposed to support achieving larger network capability, extensive continuous coverage, and enhanced spectral efficiency, which is evaluated through three representative scenarios with progressive baselines. Subsequently, a service-aware deployment strategy is introduced to further establish the engineering feasibility of the proposed architecture.

papers.title: Fast Relax-and-Round Unit Commitment with Economic Horizons
papers.summary: The US energy system is under increasing pressure to serve expanding data centers loads and to accommodate a larger number of generating units with varying technologies and ownership structures. Therefore, developing new unit commitment (UC) methods remains a priority for reliable and affordable grid operations. We expand our novel computational method for UC to include ramping constraints and long-horizon planning, and provide a theoretical bound on its accuracy. We solve problems with thousands of generators at 5-minute market intervals. We show that our method can solve UC problems with over 20,000 generators in approximately 10 seconds on commodity hardware and that an increased planning horizon leads to sizable op- erational cost savings. This is twice as fast as the leading commercial solver, Gurobi. The gap increases when adding more constraints. Our method can be implemented using existing continuous optimization solvers and adapted for different applications. We prove a bound on the error of these solvers and show that it vanishes (in relative terms) as the problem becomes larger. Our novel algorithm could allow an operator to make horizon-aware economic decisions for large systems.
